advances: The obstruction is to independent auxiliary convex fiber factors, including every integer exponential correction. It does not exclude coupled constructions.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Let the common proportionality constant be $c>0$. Convexity requires $(Q_0+Q_2)/2\subseteq Q_1$, and all three volumes would be positive. Classical Brunn–Minkowski would give
$$
c^{1/r}e^{a/r}2^{(1-k)/r}=|Q_1|^{1/r}
\ \ge\ \frac{|Q_0|^{1/r}+|Q_2|^{1/r}}2
=c^{1/r}\frac{1+e^{2a/r}}2\ge c^{1/r}e^{a/r}.
$$
This is impossible since $k>1$. The factor requirement is exactly that $v_z^k|Q_z|=c e^{az}v_z$, by multiplication of independent fiber volumes.

source_sections.locator: 7d9bc9c2dd92ae95:03 §5, auxiliary-volume correction with or without integer exponential tilt

statement: Let $v_0=v_2=1$ and $v_1=2$ be the interval lengths at the three integer bases of $\{(z,x):0\le z\le2,\ 0\le x\le2-|z-1|\}$. For every integer $k>1$, positive integer $r$, and real $a$, there is no convex auxiliary fiber family of compact sets $Q_z\subset\mathbb R^r$ on these bases with volumes proportional to $e^{az}v_z^{1-k}$ by one positive constant. Consequently independent convex factors cannot correct the $k$th-power weights back to the original weights even up to an integer exponential tilt.
title: Independent convex auxiliary fibers cannot undo a shared-integer power
